messages:
leo: Ok watercooler challenge: describe your favorite model as a dinner dish. non-serious only. :plate_with_cutlery:

anya: I'm picturing 'GPT Alfredo'  overly rich, slightly dramatic, always adds extra garlic. :garlic:

marc: 'Tiny-Ramen'  fast, comforting, sometimes misses the noodle count. :ramen:

sita: ha. prompt remix idea: feed the model a recipe prompt and see how literal it gets.

leo: mini-contest: best one-line chef-prompt wins a virtual cookie. entries here. rule: include a funny constraint.

anya: entry: ```
System: You are ChefGPT, a celebrity model-chef. Describe a sandwich in 10 words or less and include one dramatic flourish.
User: "Make me a lunchtime hero."
Assistant: "Sourdough, smoky aioli, roasted tomatoes, audaciously victorious."
```

marc: entry: "You are Sous-Edge. Only use pantry items under 50MB. No metaphor." :rofl:

sita: entry: "You are Stew-Sage. Every recipe must include exactly one life lesson and one spice pun."

chef-bot: test: deploy-prompt-kitchen failed: `error: infinite garnish loop detected` at step garnish_loop(>=3). Suggest reducing garnish recursion.

leo: ops note: don't actually run infinite creativity loops on production models. we lost an afternoon to glitter once. :grimacing:

anya: vote: do we make this a monthly 'prompt potluck' in #random? 1) yes 2) no 3) only if chef-bot behaves

marc: 1

sita: 3 (trust but verify)

leo: 1 (virtual cookies for all)

chef-bot: recorded votes and scheduled a dry-run. logs: `potluck-preview v0.3 healthy`

anya: ok I'll put a tiny banner image request in design. title: 'Prompt Potluck: Bring a dish, leave a prompt.' :tada:

marc: final silly: "If asked for code review, ChefGPT will garnish your PR with one emoji and a culinary metaphor." :sparkles:
